description: AI Knowledge curriculum: the single map every content step writes against. Lesson files live at src/content/lessons/<track>/<slug>.mdx. See research/curriculum-rationale.md for the reasoning and docs/authoring.md section 11 for the format.

conventions.minutes: Bite-sized: every lesson is 10-30 minutes of reading plus exercises.
conventions.prerequisites: Hard prerequisites only. Each one is taught earlier in the recommended order. No core or project lesson depends on a setup lesson.
conventions.exerciseTypes: Planned exercise types use the schema types: mcq, numeric, short, reveal.
conventions.sources: Lesson sources reference ids in sourceRegistry. Writers copy them into the lesson frontmatter (and may add more). Every source must be cited in the text.
conventions.needs: Software a lesson needs on your machine (python, numpy, torch, chess). Get it from the setup track or use Google Colab.

skipPaths.label: Skip setup
skipPaths.description: You already have Python 3.11+ with PyTorch, or you will use Google Colab.

skipPaths.label: I know Python and NumPy
skipPaths.description: You can write functions, classes and recursion, and you know array shapes and broadcasting.

skipPaths.label: I know the math
skipPaths.description: Vectors, matrices, derivatives, the chain rule and softmax are familiar.

skipPaths.label: Start at Intermediate
skipPaths.description: You have trained a simple model with gradient descent before.

skipPaths.label: Go straight to a project
skipPaths.description: Pick a project and read only its quickStart lessons first.

skipPolicy: Skipping only changes where the path starts and what the dashboard suggests next. It never marks lessons complete. Learners stay in full control and can mark any lesson complete themselves, which also counts towards the self-issued certificate.

certificateRequirement.description: Complete every lesson in the Beginner, Intermediate and Advanced tracks, plus every lesson of at least one project track. The Setup track is optional and never required.

tracks.title: Setup
tracks.skipNote: Optional. Skip this track if you already have Python 3.11+ (3.14 recommended), a code editor and a virtual environment with PyTorch, or if you will use Google Colab. Nothing else in the course lists a setup lesson as a prerequisite.
tracks.blurb: Install Python, VS Code and PyTorch step by step on Windows, macOS or Linux, with direct links and annotated screenshots. Or skip it and use Colab.

lessons.title: Before you start: what we install and why
goals: Name the tools the course uses (terminal, Python, VS Code, a virtual environment, PyTorch) and what each one is for
Choose between a local install and Google Colab
Decide which setup lessons you can skip
lessons.covers: Workshop analogy (bench, tools, toolbox). Install order picture. Time budget (about 45 min the first time). Skip banner: "Already have Python 3.11+? Jump to the virtual-environment lesson."

lessons.title: Open a terminal and run your first commands
goals: Open a terminal on Windows, macOS or Linux
Run cd, ls/dir and python --version and read the output
Tell the shell prompt apart from the Python prompt
lessons.covers: Windows Terminal with PowerShell, macOS Terminal via Spotlight, Linux terminal. Terminal reference table. OS tabs.

lessons.title: Install Python 3.14 on Windows, macOS or Linux
goals: Install Python 3.14 with the Python install manager (Windows), the python.org installer or Homebrew (macOS), or apt/dnf (Linux)
Avoid the Microsoft Store "python" alias trap and the deprecated-installer pitfalls
Verify the install with python --version / py --version
lessons.covers: Windows route A (install manager 26.4 MSIX) and route B (legacy installer with the PATH checkbox). macOS pkg + Install Certificates. Linux apt with python3-venv. Avoid 3.14.1 (torchvision) and 3.10 (EOL).

lessons.title: Install VS Code with the Python and Jupyter extensions
goals: Download and install VS Code for your OS
Install the Microsoft Python and Jupyter extensions and recognise the verified publisher
Open a folder and run a one-line Python file
lessons.covers: User installer x64, Add to PATH task, Extensions panel, verified-publisher trust cue, Workspace Trust.

lessons.title: Create a project folder and a virtual environment
goals: Explain what a virtual environment is and why every project gets one
Create and activate .venv on your OS (and fix the PowerShell execution-policy error)
Select the .venv interpreter in VS Code
Upgrade pip with python -m pip
lessons.covers: Folder outside OneDrive (C:\dev\ai-knowledge). python -m venv .venv, activation per shell, Set-ExecutionPolicy -Scope CurrentUser, Python: Select Interpreter, python -m pip install --upgrade pip.

lessons.title: Install PyTorch: CPU or GPU
goals: Decide between CPU and CUDA builds with the decision flowchart (NVIDIA GPU, driver >= 580)
Copy the right command from the PyTorch selector
Check torch.__version__ and torch.cuda.is_available()
lessons.covers: CPU is the course default; all projects train on a laptop CPU. CUDA 13.2/13.4 tiles. Apple-silicon MPS note; Intel Macs go to Colab. Stale-doc warnings (trust PyPI and the command table).

lessons.title: Install the other libraries and verify your setup
goals: Install NumPy, Matplotlib, Jupyter, tqdm, Pillow and chess from requirements.txt
Run verify_setup.py and read every line of its output
Know why the package is called chess, not python-chess
lessons.covers: python -m pip install -r requirements.txt; verify script prints versions, a tensor op, CUDA availability.

lessons.title: No install? Use Google Colab
goals: Open a new Colab notebook and run Python in the browser
Switch the runtime to a GPU and know the free-tier limits
Install chess with !pip and save your work to Drive
lessons.covers: Zero-install path for Intel Macs, locked-down school PCs and Chromebooks. "Open in Colab" links for companion notebooks.

lessons.title: Troubleshooting, Git and next steps
goals: Fix the most common setup errors with the FAQ (python not found, pip not found, SSL, execution policy, wrong interpreter)
Optionally install Git and GitHub Desktop to download the companion code
Know when WSL2 is worth it and when it is not
lessons.covers: 17-entry FAQ from research. Git for Windows, GitHub Desktop. WSL2 note.

tracks.title: Beginner
tracks.blurb: What AI is, the Python and NumPy you need, the math piece by piece, and your first neural network trained by hand.

lessons.title: What AI, machine learning and deep learning are
goals: Tell AI, machine learning and deep learning apart with one example each
Place the key milestones (1943 neuron, 1958 perceptron, 1986 backprop, 2012 AlexNet, 2017 Transformer) on a timeline
Name the three learning settings: supervised, unsupervised, reinforcement
Say what neural networks do ("learn patterns from data") without claiming they think
lessons.covers: Nested-circles diagram, interactive timeline, learning as function fitting (preview), AI winters, Turing Award 2018, Nobel 2024. Analogy guardrails.

lessons.title: Data, features and labels: learning as function fitting
goals: Describe a dataset as examples made of features and a label
Explain "learning" as fitting a function f(x) ≈ y with adjustable parameters
Explain why data is split into train, validation and test sets
Recognise classification versus regression
lessons.covers: House-price and digit examples, a line y = wx + b fitted by eye, the parameter as a knob, train/val/test split, data leakage preview.

lessons.title: The Python you need for machine learning
goals: Use variables, lists, dictionaries, loops and functions
Write a recursive function and trace it (used again by the chess engine)
Define a small class with __init__ and a method (used again by nn.Module)
Read a traceback and fix the error it points to
lessons.covers: Only what the course uses: list comprehensions, dict lookups, f-strings, functions with defaults, recursion (factorial and a tiny tree walk), classes, importing modules, running a .py file vs a notebook.

lessons.title: NumPy arrays, shapes and broadcasting
goals: Create arrays and read their shape and dtype
Index, slice and reshape arrays without loops
Predict the result shape of a broadcast operation step by step
Explain why vectorized code is faster than a Python loop
lessons.covers: ndarray, shape/dtype, axis argument, reshape, broadcasting micro-steps (right-align shapes, stretch 1s), copies vs views, timing a loop vs a vectorized sum.

lessons.title: Vectors and the dot product
goals: Read a vector as a list of numbers and as an arrow
Compute a dot product by hand and with NumPy
Interpret the dot product as a weighted sum and as a similarity score
lessons.covers: Shopping-basket analogy (prices × quantities), geometric view, norm, cosine similarity preview (used again by embeddings and attention).

lessons.title: Matrices and matrix multiplication
goals: Multiply a matrix by a vector and by a matrix, entry by entry
Check shape compatibility (m×n)·(n×p) → (m×p) before multiplying
See a layer of a network as one matrix multiplication plus a bias
lessons.covers: Matmul as many dot products, the shape rule, transpose, @ in NumPy, a 2×3 worked example, batch of inputs as rows.

lessons.title: Slopes and derivatives
goals: Explain a derivative as the slope of a function at a point
Estimate a derivative numerically with a small step h
Apply the power, sum and constant rules to simple functions
lessons.covers: Speedometer analogy, rise over run, (f(x+h)-f(x))/h with worked numbers, rules table, derivative of x² and of a loss curve.

lessons.title: The chain rule, partial derivatives and gradients
goals: Apply the chain rule to a composition of two or three functions
Compute partial derivatives of a function of two variables
Explain the gradient as the vector of partial derivatives that points uphill
lessons.covers: Gears analogy for the chain rule, worked example with numbers, partial derivatives holding others fixed, gradient vector, preview of backprop.

lessons.title: Probability and the softmax function
goals: Use basic probability: events, distributions that sum to 1, expectation
Turn raw scores (logits) into probabilities with softmax, step by step
Explain why subtracting the max keeps softmax numerically stable
Read the sigmoid as the two-class softmax
lessons.covers: Weather-forecast analogy, exp then normalize with worked numbers, temperature preview, log-probabilities.

lessons.title: The artificial neuron
goals: Compute a neuron's output by hand
Explain what weights, the bias and the activation do
Say why one neuron cannot learn XOR
lessons.covers: Existing sample lesson (keep). Weighted sum + bias + activation, an AND gate, the XOR limit.

lessons.title: The perceptron and activation functions
goals: Run the perceptron learning rule by hand on a tiny dataset
Explain linear separability and why XOR needs a hidden layer
Compare step, sigmoid, tanh and ReLU (shape, range, derivative)
Explain why a non-linear activation is required for depth to help
lessons.covers: Rosenblatt 1958, Minsky & Papert critique, activation plots and derivatives, vanishing-gradient preview, ReLU (Nair & Hinton 2010).

lessons.title: Loss functions: mean squared error and cross-entropy
goals: Compute mean squared error for a small batch by hand
Compute cross-entropy from softmax probabilities by hand
Choose MSE for regression and cross-entropy for classification, and say why
Read a loss value: what ln(10) ≈ 2.30 means for a 10-class guesser
lessons.covers: Darts/scorecard analogy, worked numbers, -log p of the true class, why cross-entropy punishes confident mistakes.

lessons.title: Gradient descent
goals: Explain what a gradient tells you
Run gradient-descent updates by hand
Recognise a learning rate that is too small or too large
lessons.covers: Existing sample lesson (keep). Walking downhill in fog, three updates by hand, learning-rate failure modes, stochastic/mini-batch preview.

lessons.title: Capstone: train a classifier from scratch with NumPy
goals: Assemble data, a model, a loss and gradient descent into one training loop
Train softmax regression on a small 2-D dataset in NumPy
Plot the loss curve and the decision boundary and read them
Measure accuracy on held-out data
lessons.covers: The whole beginner track in one script (about 60 lines): forward, loss, hand-derived gradient, update, evaluate. Bridge to intermediate (hidden layer, backprop).

tracks.title: Intermediate
tracks.blurb: Multilayer networks and backprop, PyTorch from tensors to training loops, and the habits that make training work.

lessons.title: Multilayer perceptrons and the forward pass
goals: Stack layers into an MLP and write its forward pass as matrix operations
Track tensor shapes through every layer of a 784→128→10 network
Count the parameters of an MLP
Explain why a hidden layer solves XOR
lessons.covers: Layer = matmul + bias + activation; XOR solved with 2 hidden units; universal approximation in plain words (with its limits); parameter counting.

lessons.title: Backpropagation, step by step
goals: Draw a computational graph and run the forward pass with numbers
Run the backward pass node by node with the chain rule
Check a hand-computed gradient against a numerical estimate
Build a tiny autograd engine (micrograd-style) that does it automatically
lessons.covers: Worked 2-layer example with numbers, local gradients × upstream gradient, gradient accumulation at forks, numerical gradient check, ~60-line Value class.

lessons.title: PyTorch tensors and autograd
goals: Create tensors, move between NumPy and PyTorch, and read shape/dtype/device
Use requires_grad and .backward() to get gradients automatically
Explain why gradients accumulate and when to zero them
Use torch.no_grad() for evaluation
lessons.covers: Tensor API mirrors NumPy; autograd reproduces the backprop lesson numbers; .grad accumulation demo; detach.

lessons.title: nn.Module, Dataset and DataLoader
goals: Define a model as an nn.Module subclass with layers and forward()
Wrap data in a Dataset and iterate it in shuffled mini-batches with a DataLoader
Inspect model.parameters() and count them
Avoid the Windows num_workers pitfall
lessons.covers: nn.Linear, nn.Sequential, custom Dataset (__len__, __getitem__), TensorDataset, batch shapes, num_workers=0 default and the __main__ guard.

lessons.title: The PyTorch training loop
goals: Write the five-line loop: forward, loss, zero_grad, backward, step
Add a validation pass with model.eval() and torch.no_grad()
Train an MLP on MNIST to about 97% and log loss per epoch
Explain what one iteration does to the numbers
lessons.covers: The canonical loop, epochs vs iterations, CrossEntropyLoss takes logits, train/eval modes, tqdm progress. Bridge to the digits project.

lessons.title: Evaluation: accuracy, precision, recall and the confusion matrix
goals: Compute accuracy, precision, recall and F1 from a confusion matrix
Explain why accuracy misleads on imbalanced data
Use the validation set for decisions and the test set only once
lessons.covers: Spam-filter example with numbers, confusion matrix reading, macro vs micro averages, scikit-learn metrics.

lessons.title: Overfitting and regularization
goals: Diagnose underfitting and overfitting from training and validation curves
Apply weight decay, dropout, early stopping and data augmentation
Explain the bias-variance trade-off in plain words, with its modern caveats
lessons.covers: Memorizing-the-answers analogy, polynomial-fit demo, L2 penalty math micro-steps, dropout at train vs eval time, Zhang et al. 2017 random-label result.

lessons.title: Optimizers: SGD, momentum, RMSProp and Adam
goals: Compare full-batch, stochastic and mini-batch gradient descent
Run momentum and Adam updates by hand for two steps
Choose an optimizer and a starting learning rate, and use a schedule
lessons.covers: Ball-rolling analogy for momentum, per-parameter step sizes, bias correction in Adam, AdamW, learning-rate schedules and warmup.

lessons.title: Initialization and normalization
goals: Explain vanishing and exploding activations with a numeric example
Use Xavier/Glorot and Kaiming/He initialization and say when
Explain what batch normalization and layer normalization do, and their train/eval difference
lessons.covers: Variance through layers micro-steps, nn.init, BatchNorm math, why LayerNorm is used in Transformers, Santurkar caveat.

lessons.title: Hyperparameters and how to tune them
goals: Tell parameters from hyperparameters
Run a learning-rate range test and a small random search
Tune in the right order with a fixed budget, using the validation set
lessons.covers: The tuning playbook's incremental strategy, LR range test (Smith 2015), batch size vs learning rate, logging experiments.

lessons.title: Debugging neural network training
goals: Follow a debugging checklist: overfit one batch, check the initial loss, visualize inputs
Spot common bugs: softmax before CrossEntropyLoss, missing zero_grad, wrong shapes, eval mode
Use gradient checks and gradient clipping
lessons.covers: Karpathy's recipe, expected initial loss ln(C), NaN hunting, gradcheck, clip_grad_norm_, a "find the bug" exercise.

lessons.title: Saving, loading and reusing models
goals: Save and load a state_dict and a full training checkpoint (model, optimizer, epoch)
Resume training from a checkpoint
Load safely with weights_only and switch to eval mode for inference
lessons.covers: torch.save/torch.load, state_dict vs whole model, checkpoint dict, map_location for CPU, reproducibility (seeds).

tracks.title: Advanced
tracks.blurb: Convolutions, sequence models, attention and Transformers, tokenization, game-tree search and self-play, and shipping models efficiently.

lessons.title: Convolutional neural networks
goals: Compute a convolution output by hand on a small image
Use the output-size formula with padding and stride
Explain weight sharing, receptive fields and pooling
Count the parameters of a small CNN
lessons.covers: Sliding-stencil analogy, worked 5×5 example (Y11), output-size drills, channels, max pooling, the 421,642-parameter digits CNN.

lessons.title: Deep CNNs: from LeNet to ResNet
goals: Trace the LeNet-5 → AlexNet → ResNet story and what each changed
Explain residual connections and why they make very deep networks trainable
Use batch normalization and global average pooling in a CNN
lessons.covers: Landmark table, degradation problem, skip connection as a highway, BatchNorm2d, global average pooling (Lin et al. 2013).

lessons.title: Embeddings and neural language models
goals: Explain one-hot vectors and why learned embeddings replace them
Describe the Bengio-style MLP language model (context → embeddings → hidden → softmax)
Measure similarity between embeddings with the dot product and cosine
lessons.covers: nn.Embedding as a lookup table = one-hot × matrix, Bengio 2003, word2vec idea, makemore MLP shapes.

lessons.title: Recurrent networks: RNN, LSTM and GRU
goals: Unroll an RNN over time and compute one step by hand
Explain vanishing gradients through time
Walk through the LSTM gates with scalar numbers
Use nn.LSTM / nn.GRU and get the shapes right
lessons.covers: Hidden state as a notebook, BPTT, Bengio 1994, LSTM gates (forget/input/output), GRU, char-rnn.

lessons.title: Attention, step by step
goals: Compute scaled dot-product attention by hand for three tokens
Explain queries, keys and values with the library analogy
Apply a causal mask and explain why it is needed
Explain why we divide by √d
lessons.covers: Bahdanau 2014 motivation (bottleneck), the 3-token table worked example, self-attention, causal masking, multi-head.

lessons.title: The Transformer and GPT
goals: Draw a decoder-only Transformer block (attention, MLP, residuals, LayerNorm)
Explain positional embeddings and weight tying
Count the parameters of a tiny GPT
Estimate training compute with 6 × params × tokens
lessons.covers: Block diagram, pre-LN, GELU, GPT-2 recipe, nanoGPT config table, scaling-law estimate.

lessons.title: Tokenization and byte-pair encoding
goals: Compare character, word and subword tokenization
Run BPE merges by hand on a tiny corpus
Explain byte-level BPE and why vocabulary size is a trade-off
Avoid tokenizer leakage (train it on training data only)
lessons.covers: The worked BPE example, encode/decode round trip, tiktoken demo, vocab size vs model size.

lessons.title: Language modelling, perplexity and sampling
goals: Explain next-token prediction and the shifted-target trick
Convert loss to perplexity and read it
Apply temperature, top-k and top-p (nucleus) sampling by hand
Explain why greedy decoding repeats itself
lessons.covers: y = x[1:] alignment, loss in nats per token, perplexity, sampling micro-steps with numbers, degeneration (Holtzman 2019).

lessons.title: Game-tree search: minimax and alpha-beta
goals: Build a game tree and score it with minimax by hand
Rewrite minimax as negamax
Prune a tree with alpha-beta and count the nodes saved
Explain why move ordering makes pruning stronger
lessons.covers: Tic-tac-toe example, hiker analogy (search vs evaluation), flight-shopping analogy for alpha-beta, Knuth & Moore best case.

lessons.title: Reinforcement learning and self-play: an overview
goals: Define agent, environment, state, action, reward and policy
Explain how AlphaZero combines a policy/value network with tree search (MCTS) and self-play
Contrast the AlphaZero/Leela approach with Stockfish's alpha-beta + NNUE approach
lessons.covers: Overview only (no RL code): Samuel 1959 checkers, AlphaGo, AlphaZero, Leela; why our chess project uses supervised learning on Stockfish evaluations instead.

lessons.title: Transfer learning and fine-tuning
goals: Explain why features learned on one task transfer to another
Fine-tune a pretrained torchvision model: freeze, replace the head, train
Choose between feature extraction and full fine-tuning
lessons.covers: Yosinski 2014 layer-transfer findings, torchvision weights API, learning rates for the head vs the body, when transfer hurts.

lessons.title: Efficient inference: quantization, pruning and export
goals: Explain int8 quantization with a scale and zero-point, by hand
Measure model size and latency before and after dynamic quantization
Name other speed-ups (pruning, distillation, ONNX export, incremental updates) and their trade-offs
lessons.covers: Quantization micro-steps, torch.ao dynamic quantization demo, Deep Compression, distillation, ONNX, NNUE int16/int8 as a real-world example.

tracks.title: Handwritten digits and letters
tracks.blurb: Recognise handwritten digits (MNIST) and letters (EMNIST), then draw your own and let the model read them.
tracks.outcome: A CNN at about 99% on MNIST and about 92-94% on EMNIST letters, plus a drawing app that reads your handwriting.

lessons.title: Meet MNIST: loading and looking at handwritten digits
goals: Download MNIST with torchvision and inspect shapes, labels and pixel ranges
Normalize with the dataset mean and standard deviation
Plot a grid of samples and explain how MNIST was centred
lessons.covers: History (LeCun, Cortes, Burges), 60k/10k split, 28×28, centre-of-mass centring, licence wording.

lessons.title: An MLP baseline for MNIST
goals: Train a 784→128→10 MLP to about 97-98% test accuracy
Use the training script with --smoke and full runs
Record a baseline to compare the CNN against
lessons.covers: Flattening images, the training loop applied, expected numbers, timing on CPU.

lessons.title: A CNN that reads digits at 99%
goals: Build the 2-conv CNN and verify its 421,642 parameters
Train it to about 99% and compare with the MLP baseline
Fix the missing-channel-dimension error
lessons.covers: Conv → ReLU → MaxPool ×2 → FC, parameter arithmetic, unsqueeze(1), where 95% of parameters sit.

lessons.title: Evaluating the digit model: confusion matrix and mistakes
goals: Compute per-class accuracy and a confusion matrix
Show the most confidently wrong test images
Explain why some errors are label noise
lessons.covers: Confusion matrix plot, top-k mistakes gallery, model.eval() and no_grad.

lessons.title: From digits to letters with EMNIST
goals: Load EMNIST letters and fix its transposed orientation
Shift labels from 1-26 to 0-25
Train the 26-class CNN to about 92-94% and explain the accuracy ceiling (i/l, g/q)
Handle a failed download with the manual fallback
lessons.covers: 145,600 images, 26 merged-case classes, the two quirks, ~560 MB download, label noise and Bayes error.

lessons.title: Capstone: draw a digit or letter and let your model read it
goals: Build a tkinter drawing canvas that sends your drawing to the saved model
Preprocess the drawing exactly like the training data (crop, 20×20, centre of mass, polarity)
Explain distribution shift and why skipping preprocessing breaks a 99% model
lessons.covers: Canvas → PIL → 28×28 pipeline, loading the checkpoint, top-3 predictions with probabilities, distribution-shift callout.

tracks.title: Doodle recognition
tracks.blurb: Classify quick sketches from Google's Quick, Draw! dataset and build a live guessing app.
tracks.outcome: A CNN at about 88-93% on 10 doodle classes and a canvas app that guesses what you draw.

lessons.title: The Quick, Draw! dataset: streaming 10 classes of doodles
goals: Explain the dataset (50M drawings, 345 classes) and its CC BY 4.0 attribution rule
Download only the first N drawings per class with an HTTP Range request
Load .npy bitmaps with mmap_mode and build a balanced train/test split
lessons.covers: 10-class subset (apple … umbrella), 10k/2k per class, ~9.4 MB per class via Range, bounding-box centring vs MNIST centre of mass, content warning.

lessons.title: Training a doodle classifier
goals: Adapt the CNN to 10 doodle classes and train it on CPU
Compare its accuracy with the digits model and explain the gap
Track train and validation curves per epoch
lessons.covers: Same CNN family, expected 88-93%, why sketches are harder than digits.

lessons.title: Data augmentation and regularization for sketches
goals: Add small shifts, rotations and scaling as augmentation
Add dropout and batch normalization and measure the effect
Run a controlled before/after comparison on the validation set
lessons.covers: torchvision transforms on tensors, which augmentations keep the label (small shifts, rotations and scaling do; large rotations can turn shapes into other classes), one-variable-at-a-time experiments.

lessons.title: Reading the confusion matrix: which doodles get mixed up
goals: Plot the 10×10 confusion matrix and find the most confused pairs
Inspect misclassified drawings and judge whether the label or the model is wrong
Predict how accuracy changes with more or more similar classes
lessons.covers: Instructive errors between classes with similar outlines (measure which pairs on your own run instead of assuming), adding a look-alike class as an experiment, 345-class reality check.

lessons.title: Capstone: a live doodle-guessing app
goals: Build a canvas app that guesses while you draw
Preprocess strokes like Quick, Draw! (bounding box, margin, line width, antialiased downsample)
Show top-3 guesses with probabilities and explain confidence vs correctness
lessons.covers: Preprocessing that differs from MNIST (no centre of mass), live prediction loop, credit line "Quick, Draw! dataset by Google, CC BY 4.0".

tracks.title: Small-text models
tracks.blurb: Generate names and Shakespeare-like text character by character, then classify the sentiment of short sentences.
tracks.outcome: A name generator (bigram → MLP), a character-level LSTM that writes Shakespeare-like text, and a sentiment classifier at about 78-84% on SST-2.

lessons.title: A bigram name generator from counts
goals: Count character pairs in 32,033 names and turn counts into probabilities
Sample new names from the bigram table
Compute the average negative log-likelihood and compare with the uniform 3.30
lessons.covers: 27-symbol vocabulary with a start/end token, smoothing, loss 3.30 → ~2.45, a first "language model".

lessons.title: A neural name generator (Bengio-style MLP)
goals: Build the context-3 MLP with 10-dimensional embeddings (11,897 parameters)
Train it and beat the bigram dev loss (~2.1-2.2)
Sample names and judge them
lessons.covers: Dataset of (context, next char) pairs, embedding lookup, train/dev/test split, overfitting check.

lessons.title: A character-level Shakespeare generator with an LSTM
goals: Prepare TinyShakespeare (1.1M characters, 65 symbols) with a 90/10 split
Train a char-level LSTM with truncated backpropagation through time
Sample with temperature and read the output critically
Compare against the tiny GPT from the code track (stretch)
lessons.covers: char-rnn approach, batching long text into chunks, hidden-state carry-over, gradient clipping, val loss in nats per character.

lessons.title: Short texts: preparing SST-2 movie-review sentences
goals: Download the SST-2 zip and read the tab-separated sentences
Build a word vocabulary from the training split only, with <unk> and <pad>
Pad and batch variable-length sentences
lessons.covers: 67,349 train / 872 validation (used as test), carving a validation set from train, licence and citation note, vocabulary leakage.

lessons.title: A bag-of-embeddings sentiment classifier
goals: Build Embedding → mean-pool → Linear and train it on CPU
Reach about 78-82% validation accuracy and report precision/recall
Find sentences it gets wrong because word order is ignored ("not good")
lessons.covers: Mean pooling with a padding mask, ~1M parameters mostly in embeddings, error analysis.

lessons.title: Capstone: a BiLSTM classifier for your own sentences
goals: Upgrade to a 1-layer bidirectional LSTM and compare with the bag-of-embeddings model
Save the model and classify sentences you type
Explain what scale buys (GLUE baselines vs fine-tuned Transformers above 93%)
lessons.covers: Packed sequences or masking, final hidden states of both directions, predict.py CLI, IMDB as an optional longer-text challenge.

tracks.title: Code autocompletion
tracks.blurb: Train a tiny GPT on Python's own standard library and use it to complete code.
tracks.outcome: A ~1.8M-parameter character-level GPT (then a BPE version) that completes Python, measured by validation loss in bits per character and the parse rate of its completions.

lessons.title: Building a code corpus from Python's standard library
goals: Find the standard library with sysconfig and collect about 10 MB of .py files
Clean it: skip tests, normalize line endings and tabs, add file separators
Explain the PSF licence and why we never ship the corpus or weights
lessons.covers: No download needed, measured counts (568 non-test files / ≈9.7M characters on CPython 3.13 for Windows), fixed 97-character alphabet, train/val split by file.

lessons.title: Writing a tiny GPT in PyTorch
goals: Implement embeddings, causal self-attention, the MLP block and the LM head
Check every tensor shape with a tiny config
Count parameters for the 4-layer, d=192 model (~1.8M)
lessons.covers: One-file model (~150 lines) modelled on nanoGPT/minGPT, causal mask via scaled_dot_product_attention(is_causal=True), weight tying.

lessons.title: Training the code model on a CPU
goals: Run training with random context windows, AdamW and a cosine schedule
Estimate the compute budget (6 × params × tokens) and the run time
Save checkpoints and resume; spot the "forgot the causal mask" bug from a near-zero loss
lessons.covers: About 1 hour CPU run (4,000 steps), --smoke mode, eval every N steps, loss in nats per token and bits per character, --resume and the --no-causal-mask demo.

lessons.title: Sampling completions and measuring the parse rate
goals: Complete a code prompt with temperature and top-k sampling
Measure the fraction of generated functions that parse with ast.parse
Explain why longer completions drift
lessons.covers: Prompt cropping to block_size, stop conditions (blank line, dedent), parse-rate metric, qualitative review.

lessons.title: Stage 2: a BPE tokenizer for code
goals: Train a BPE vocabulary (a few hundred merges, scalable to 2-4k tokens) on the training files only
Retrain the model on BPE tokens and compare loss per character fairly
Explain the vocabulary-size versus model-size trade-off
lessons.covers: minbpe-style trainer, bits-per-character comparison across tokenizers, whitespace/indentation tokens.

lessons.title: Capstone: a command-line autocomplete tool
goals: Wrap the model in a CLI that completes the code you paste
Speed up inference with no_grad, eval mode, thread settings and dynamic quantization, and measure the latency
State honestly what a 2M-parameter model can and cannot do compared with large code models
lessons.covers: complete.py CLI, latency measurement, quantized vs float output comparison, limitations.

tracks.title: Mini chess engine
tracks.blurb: Build a mini-Stockfish: alpha-beta search with a neural-network evaluator trained on Lichess positions, speaking UCI.
tracks.outcome: A Python UCI engine with alpha-beta, quiescence, iterative deepening and a transposition table, using a 768→256→32→1 network as its evaluator, with a measured Elo estimate against Stockfish at limited strength.
tracks.quickStartNote: Lessons 1-5 (the classic engine) only need python-for-ml and game-tree-search, so you can start the engine right away and pick up the deep-learning lessons before lesson 6.

lessons.title: Boards, moves and perft with python-chess
goals: Read and write positions in FEN
Generate legal moves and make/unmake them with push/pop
Write a perft function and confirm perft(3) = 8,902 from the start position
lessons.covers: Milestone 1. Install chess (not python-chess), board representation overview, the exponential tree.

lessons.title: Material and piece-square tables
goals: Write a material evaluation in centipawns
Add piece-square tables and explain what they encode
Return scores from the side to move's point of view and test the sign with a mirrored position
lessons.covers: Milestone 2. evaluate(board) as the single swap point for the later network, eval(start) = 0, knight removed = −320.

lessons.title: Negamax search with alpha-beta pruning
goals: Implement negamax with alpha-beta on real chess positions
Handle checkmate (−MATE + ply), stalemate and repetition draws
Count nodes and confirm the same best move as plain minimax
Solve mate-in-2 puzzles at depth 4
lessons.covers: Milestone 3. Node counting as the yardstick for every later improvement, Lichess puzzle test set (CC0).

lessons.title: Move ordering and quiescence search
goals: Order moves with MVV-LVA, killer moves and the history heuristic
Measure a 5× or larger drop in nodes at depth 4
Explain the horizon effect and fix it with a captures-only quiescence search
lessons.covers: Milestones 4-5. Detective line-up and photographer analogies, stand-pat score, horizon-trap test FENs.

lessons.title: Iterative deepening, Zobrist hashing and a transposition table
goals: Search deeper one ply at a time within a time budget
Hash positions with Zobrist keys and store results in a transposition table with bound types
Adjust mate scores by ply when storing and probing the table
lessons.covers: Milestone 6. Exam-answered-roughly-then-refined analogy, fingerprint dabbing (Zobrist), dict TT capped at 1-2M entries, movetime respect, pitfall d4.2.

lessons.title: A training set from the Lichess evaluation database
goals: Stream positions from the Lichess evaluation export (CC0) without downloading everything
Pick the deepest evaluation, convert White-relative cp to side-to-move, and skip mates and non-quiet positions
Encode positions as 768 piece-square features and save 1-2M samples compactly
lessons.covers: Milestone 7. jsonl.zst streaming with python-zstandard or the Hugging Face Parquet slices, filtering rules, feature indices.

lessons.title: Training the 768→256→32→1 evaluator
goals: Build the network with EmbeddingBag as a sparse first layer and ClippedReLU
Train in win-draw-loss space (sigmoid of cp / 400) with Adam on CPU
Sanity-check the net: start position near 0 to +50 cp, queen up ≫ 0, mirrored position negated
lessons.covers: Milestone 8. Why WDL-space loss, appraiser vs sale prices analogy, 20-60 min CPU training, validation curves.

lessons.title: Plugging the network into search (and the NNUE idea)
goals: Run the network in NumPy inside search and keep quiescence in front of it
Explain the NNUE accumulator: update 2-4 columns per move instead of recomputing
Run a 100-game match against the piece-square engine and read the Elo and its error bars
lessons.covers: Milestone 9 + optional upgrade (c). Running-bank-balance analogy, two perspectives, honest 1.2-2× Python speed-up, quantization as stretch.

lessons.title: Capstone: a UCI engine and an Elo estimate against Stockfish
goals: Implement the UCI commands (uci, isready, position, go, stop, quit) with safe time management
Pass a fastchess compliance check and play in a GUI
Estimate Elo with error bars against Stockfish UCI_Elo anchors and explain SPRT
State which numbers are estimates and how to measure your own
lessons.covers: Milestone 10. Move overhead margin, fastchess matches, Elo from score, ±70 Elo at 100 games, GPL note for python-chess.
